messages:
jess: Quick favor — can someone run a small-window continuous-batching pass with 3 payload variants (short, med, long)? Prod p95 jumped after the last rollout and I want to rule out queuing path changes.

liam: I can kick one off. Which model + max_tokens target?

jess: Use rdx-3b-qual (the canary), try max_tokens=64 and 256. Also include a run with `--prefer-small-batches` off to compare. We suspect the windowing heuristic might be grouping short prompts into larger batches incorrectly.

liam: Got it. I'll run loadgen with the following:

```
./loadgen --model rdx-3b-qual --concurrency 32 --seq-dist short,med,long --max-tokens 64,256 --warmup 60 --duration 300 --tag small-window-probe-195123
```

liam: Starting job now (job id job-195123-A). Will post perf CI links when finished.

anya: Quick Q — do we want prefix/KV caching enabled? That can change batch formation for short prompts.

jess: Yes, enable caching for the default run and a separate run with caching disabled. Add `--kv-cache on|off`.

mike: Heads-up: if the batching window shrinks too much, we might see higher GPU kernel overhead per-token. Watch p50 vs p95 divergence.

perf-ci-bot: job-195123-A started by liam — small-window-probe-195123 (runtimes: rdx-3b-qual)

liam: Two runs done (cache=on, cache=off). Uploading flamegraphs and raw traces to: https://perfci.internal/reports/job-195123-A

perf-ci-bot: job-195123-A completed — summary: p50=42ms p95=198ms p99=420ms (cache=on, max_tokens=64). Detailed: https://perfci.internal/reports/job-195123-A/summary

jess: Thanks. Can you also run the same with `max_batch_tokens=8192` and `max_batch_items=8` to test cap behavior? A hypothesis is that long seqs push token caps and force smaller item batches.

liam: Running job-195123-B with those caps. Adding `--collect-queue-stats` and `--emit-batch-histogram`.

liam: job-195123-B done — report: https://perfci.internal/reports/job-195123-B. Observations: when max_batch_tokens=8192 we still see 3x p95 regression on short prompts vs baseline. Batch hist shows a lot of 1-item batches for short-seq workload.

anya: If 1-item batches dominate, we should check the window expiration timer. It might be too low. What's the current window_ms for this canary?

mike: Current window_ms=8ms in canary. For short prompts at concurrency=32 that might be preempting aggregation. Try bumping to 20ms and re-run synthetic.

jess: Good catch. liam, can you run a targeted run toggling window_ms 8/12/20 with short-only payload? Keep max_tokens=64.

liam: Will do. job-195123-C started — short-only sweep, window_ms=[8,12,20].

perf-ci-bot: job-195123-C completed — artifacts: https://perfci.internal/reports/job-195123-C. Summary: window_ms=8 -> p95 210ms; 12 -> 150ms; 20 -> 130ms. Batch hist: 8ms -> 60% 1-item batches; 20ms -> 85% 4-8 item batches.

jess: Looks like increasing window reduces p95 as expected. Next step: quantify cost impact and check tail latencies under real traffic pattern. Can we run a mixed-prod-like trace replay (from trace-id 2024-10-12-prodwave) with window_ms=20 and compare cost tokens/sec?

liam: I can replay trace, but need sign-off to use the production trace. @anya can you approve?

anya: Approved for perf runs only. Make sure the trace is anonymized.

liam: Kicked off job-195123-D (trace replay). perf-ci-bot will post when done.

perf-ci-bot: job-195123-D completed — replay report: https://perfci.internal/reports/job-195123-D. Replay notes: p95 down 28% vs baseline, tokens/sec slightly up (1.05x). No increase in GPU time per token.

mike: This is promising. Would like a lightweight canary in staging for 24h with window_ms=20 and autoscale set to current policy to surface any interaction with real routing.

jess: Agreed. I'll open a small rollout PR to staging config (PR #4120) with window_ms override and the canary label. liam please attach the perf links to the PR and add an explicit rollback tag.

liam: PR #4120 created: https://git.internal/repo/runtimes/PR-4120 — description + links to job-195123-{A,B,C,D}. Adding `rollback: immediate` flag.

anya: I'll monitor logs and tail p95 during the 24h staging canary. If anything >2x baseline, I'll hit rollback.

jess: Sweet. Thanks team. Quick follow-up: can someone write a short note for the runbook about window_ms tuning and the tradeoffs we saw? Two bullet points should suffice.

mike: I'll add a blurb to runbook: "Increase window_ms to improve aggregation for short prompts — reduces p95 at cost of slightly higher batching latency; validate tokens/sec and GPU time per token during replay." Will link to these perf artifacts.

liam: Closing loop: uploaded all raw traces to s3://rdx-perf/job-195123/ and added filenames in PR.

jess: Awesome. Closing thread — will check back after staging canary. :thumbsup:
